s.d: a Roman mile, milliarium , = 1000 paces,= 8 stades, = 1680 yards, i. e. 80 yards less than our mile, (Polybius Historicus), etc. (ML)

μιμέομαι, -οῦμαι (μῖμος, a mimic, an actor), [in LXX: [[psalms 31 6|Psa.31:6]], Wis.4:2 15:9, 4Ma.9:23 4Mac 9:13 : * ;] to imitate: [[2-thessalonians 3 7|2Th.3:7 3:9]] [[hebrews 13 7|Heb.13:7]], 3Jn.11.† (AS)

[[ezekiel 18 22|Eze.18:22]]), [[acts 10 31|Act.10:31]], [[revelation 16 19|Rev.16:19]] (cf. ἀνα-, ἐπ-ανα-, ὑπο- μιμνήσκω. The tenses of this verb are from the older μνάομαι).† (AS)

μισέω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for שָׂנֵא ;] to hate: with accusative of person(s) [[matthew 5 43|Mat.5:43 24:10]], [[luke 1 71|Luk.1:71 6:22, 27 19:14]], [[john 7 7|Jhn.7:7 15:18-19, 23-26 17:14]], [[titus 3 3|Tit.3:3]], [[1-john 2 9|1Jn.2:9]] [[john 2 11|Jn 2:11]] [[john 3 13|Jn 3:13]] [[john 3 15|Jn 3:15]] [[john 4 20|Jn 4:20]] [[revelation 17 16|Rev.17:16]]; pass., [[matthew 10 22|Mat.10:22 24:9]], [[mark 13 13|Mrk.13:13]], [[luke 21 17|Luk.21:17]]; with accusative of thing(s), [[john 3 20|Jhn.3:20]], [[romans 7 15|Rom.7:15]], [[ephesians 5 29|Eph.5:29]], [[hebrews 1 9|Heb.1:9]], Ju 23, [[revelation 2 6|Rev.2:6]]; pass., [[revelation 18 2|Rev.18:2.]] As the Heb. שָׂנֵא is sometimes found with the modified sense of indifference to or relative disregard for one thing in comparison with another (cf. [[genesis 29 30|Gen.29:30-31]], [[deuteronomy 21 15|Deu.21:15-16]], [[malachi 1 3|Mal.1:3]]) so prob. μ. in the foll.: [[matthew 6 24|Mat.6:24]], [[luke 14 26|Luk.14:26 16:13]], [[john 12 25|Jhn.12:25]], [[romans 9 13|Rom.9:13]]" (LXX) .† (AS)
μισθαποδοσία, -ας, ἡ (μισθός, ἀποδίδωμι; cl. μισθοδοσία), pay­ment of wages, recompense; meton., (a) of reward: [[hebrews 10 35|Heb.10:35 11:26]]; (b) of punishment : [[hebrews 2 2|Heb.2:2.]]† (AS)
μισθ-απο-δότης, -ου, ὁ (see supr.), one who pays wages; meton., a rewarder: [[hebrews 11 6|Heb.11:6.]]† (AS)

μίσθιος, -α, -ον (also -ος, -ον), [in LXX: [[leviticus 19 13|Lev.19:13]] A [[leviticus 25 50|Lev.25:50]], [[job 7 1|Job.7:1]] (שָׂכִיר), Tob.5:11, Sir.7:10 31:22 37:11 * ;] hired; as subst., ὁ μ., a hired servant: [[luke 15 17|Luk.15:17, 19 15:21]] (Anth., Plut.).† (AS)

μισθός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for שָׂכָר ;] 1. prop., wages, hire: [[matthew 20 8|Mat.20:8]], [[luke 10 7|Luk.10:7]], [[romans 4 4|Rom.4:4]], [[1-timothy 5 18|1Ti.5:18]], [[james 5 4|Jas.5:4]], Ju 11; μ. ἀδικίας, [[acts 1 18|Act.1:18]], [[2-peter 2 13|2Pe.2:13]] (but see Mayor and ICC, in l), [[2-peter 2 15|2Pe.2:15.]] 2. Generally, reward: [[john 4 36|Jhn.4:36]], [[1-corinthians 9 18|1Co.9:18]]; esp. of divine rewards, [[matthew 5 12|Mat.5:12 6:1-2, 5 6:16 10:41-42]] [[mark 9 41|Mrk.9:41]], [[luke 6 23|Luk.6:23, 35]], [[1-corinthians 3 8|1Co.3:8 3:14]], 2Jn.8, [[revelation 11 18|Rev.11:18 22:12]]; ἔχειν μ., [[matthew 5 46|Mat.5:46]], [[1-corinthians 9 17|1Co.9:17]].† (AS)
μισθόω, -ῶ (μισθός) [in LXX (mid.) chiefly for שָׂכָר ;] to let out for hire. Mid., to hire: with accusative, [[matthew 20 1|Mat.20:1]], 7.† (AS)

μίσθωμα, -τος, τό (μισθόω), [in LXX: [[deuteronomy 23 18|Deu.23:18]] (19), [[micah 1 7|Mic.1:7]], [[ezekiel 16 31|Eze.16:31, 34 16:41]] (אֶתְנַן), [[ezekiel 16 33|Eze.16:33]], (נֵדֶה, נָדָן), [[ezekiel 16 32|Eze.16:32]], [[proverbs 19 13|Pro.19:13]] * ;] 1. price, hire (cl, and LXX). 2. In sense not found elsewhere, a hired dwelling: [[acts 28 30|Act.28:30.]]† (AS)
μισθωτός, -ή, όν (μισθόω), [in LXX for שָׂכִיר, [[exodus 12 45|Exo.12:45]], al. ;] hired; as subst., ὁ μ., a hired servant, hireling: [[mark 1 20|Mrk.1:20]], [[john 10 12|Jhn.10:12-13]].† (AS)
Μιτυλήνη, -ης, ἡ (late form - Strab., Plut. - of cl. Μυτιλ-), Mytilene, Mitylene, chief city of Lesbos: [[acts 20 14|Act.20:14.]]† (AS)
Μιχαήλ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. מִיכָאֵל, who like God?), Michael, the Archangel (cf. [[daniel 12 1|Dan.12:1]]) : Ju 9, [[revelation 12 7|Rev.12:7]].† (AS)

μνᾶ, -ᾶς, ἡ (a Semitic word; cf. Heb. מָנֶה, Aram. מְנֵא, a weight and a sum of money = 100 shekels, cf. [[1-kings 10 17|3Ki.10:17]]), a mina (Let.), mna, in Attic a weight and sum of money = 100 δραχμαί (which see) : [[luke 19 13|Luk.19:13, 16 19:18, 20 19:24-25]].† (AS)

[[ezekiel 18 22|Eze.18:22]]), [[acts 10 31|Act.10:31]], [[revelation 16 19|Rev.16:19]] (cf. ἀνα-, ἐπ-ανα-, ὑπο- μιμνήσκω. The tenses of this verb are from the older μνάομαι).† (AS)
Μνάσων, -ωνος, ὁ Mnason: [[acts 21 16|Act.21:16.]]† (AS)

μνεία, -ας, ἡ (μιμνήσκω), [in LXX for זָכַר, its parts and deriva­tives ;] remembrance, mention (= μνήμη) : [[philippians 1 3|Php.1:3;]] μ. ποιεῖσθαι, with genitive of person(s), [[romans 1 9|Rom.1:9]], [[ephesians 1 16|Eph.1:16]], [[1-thessalonians 1 2|1Th.1:2]], Phm 4 (cf. [[psalms 111 4|Psa.111:4]]); μ. ἔχειν, with genitive of person(s), [[1-thessalonians 3 6|1Th.3:6]], [[2-timothy 1 3|2Ti.1:3]] (on the seel. in [[romans 12 13|Rom.12:13]], see ICC, in I.; Field, Notes, 163).† (AS)

μνῆμα, -τος, τό (μνάομαι), [in LXX for קֶבֶר, קְבוּרָה ;] 1. a memorial. 2. a sepulchral monument, a sepulchre, tomb: [[mark 5 3|Mrk.5:3, 5 15:46 16:2]] (WH, μνημεῖον), [[luke 8 27|Luk.8:27 23:53 24:1]], [[acts 2 29|Act.2:29 7:16]], [[revelation 11 9|Rev.11:9]].† SYN.: μνημεῖον (AS)

μνημεῖον, -ου, τό [in LXX for קֶבֶר, קְבוּרָה ;] 1. a memorial, record (cl., cf. Wis.10:7). 2. (a) (cl.) a monument: [[luke 11 47|Luk.11:47;]] (b) a sepulchre, tomb ([[genesis 23 6|Gen.23:6]], 9, [[isaiah 22 16|Isa.22:16]], al.): [[matthew 23 29|Mat.23:29]], [[mark 5 2|Mrk.5:2]], [[luke 11 44|Luk.11:44]], [[john 5 28|Jhn.5:28]], and frequently in Gospels, [[acts 13 29|Act.13:29]] SYN.: μνῆμα (AS)

μνήμη, -ης, ἡ (μνάομαι), [in LXX for זֵכֶר, זִכְרוֹן ;] memory, remembrance, mention: μ. ποιεῖσθαι, with genitive, to remember, [[2-peter 1 15|2Pe.1:15]] (but in cl., π., μ. π. more frequently = to make mention, and so perh. here, cf. Mayor, in l; and for ex. from π., see Zorell, see word).† SYN.: μνεία, q.v (AS)

μνημονεύω (μνήμων, mindful) [in LXX for זָכַר ;] 1. to call to mind, remember : absol., [[mark 8 18|Mrk.8:18;]] with genitive of person(s), [[luke 17 32|Luk.17:32]], [[colossians 4 18|Col.4:18]], [[1-thessalonians 1 3|1Th.1:3]], [[hebrews 11 15|Heb.11:15]] (but see infr.) [[hebrews 13 7|Heb.13:7;]] τ. πτωχῶν, [[galatians 2 20|Gal.2:20;]] with genitive of thing(s), [[john 15 20|Jhn.15:20 16:4, 21]], [[acts 20 35|Act.20:35]]; with accusative obj. (as more frequently in cl.), of persons, [[2-timothy 2 8|2Ti.2:8;]] of things, [[matthew 16 9|Mat.16:9]], [[1-thessalonians 2 9|1Th.2:9]], [[revelation 18 5|Rev.18:5]]; before ὅτι, [[acts 20 31|Act.20:31]], [[ephesians 2 11|Eph.2:11]], [[2-thessalonians 2 5|2Th.2:5]]; πόθεν, [[revelation 2 5|Rev.2:5;]] πῶς, [[revelation 3 3|Rev.3:3.]] 2. to make mention of: with genitive, [[hebrews 11 15|Heb.11:15]] (but see supr., and cf. M, Th., I, 18); before περί, [[hebrews 11 22|Heb.11:22.]]† (AS)

μνημόσυνον, -ου, τό (μνήμων, mindful), [in LXX frequently for זֵכֶר, זִכְרוֹן and cogn. forms ;] a memorial: [[matthew 26 13|Mat.26:13]], [[mark 14 9|Mrk.14:9]], [[acts 10 4|Act.10:4]] (where cf. [[leviticus 2 9|Lev.2:9, 16 5:12]], Num_5:28, Sir.45:16, al.).† (AS)

μνηστεύω [in LXX for אָרַשׂ pi., pu. ;] 1. to woo and win, espouse. 2. to promise in marriage, betroth; pass., of the woman, to be be­trothed: with dative of person(s), [[matthew 1 18|Mat.1:18]], [[luke 1 27|Luk.1:27 2:5]].† (AS)
μογι-λάλος, -ον (μόγις, λάλος), [in LXX: [[isaiah 35 6|Isa.35:6]] (אִלֵּם) * ;] speaking with difficulty: [[mark 7 32|Mrk.7:32]] (Tr., txt., μογγιλάλος, thick-voiced, see Swete, in l).† (AS)
μόγις adv. (μόγος, toil), [in LXX: Wis.9:16 א A (μόγις, B), 3Ma.7:6 * ;] with toil or difficulty, hardly: [[luke 9 39|Luk.9:39]] (μόγις, WH).† (AS)

μοιχαλίς, -ίδος, ἡ (= Att.. μοιχάς, fem. of μοιχός), [in LXX: [[proverbs 18 22|Pro.18:22]] 30:20), [[ezekiel 16 38|Eze.16:38 23:45]], [[hosea 3 1|Hos.3:1]], [[malachi 3 5|Mal.3:5]] (נַאֲפוּף, נָאַף) * ;] an adulteress: [[romans 7 3|Rom.7:3;]] meton., for μοιχεία, [[2-peter 2 14|2Pe.2:14.]] Metaphorical, of infidelity to God (cf. [[ezekiel 16 15|Eze.16:15]] ff. [[ezekiel 23 43|Eze.23:43]] ff., al.), [[james 4 4|Jas.4:4]]; as an adj., [[matthew 12 39|Mat.12:39 16:4]], [[mark 8 8|Mrk.8:8]].† (AS)

ἐγώ, genitive, etc., ἐμοῦ, ἐμοί, ἐμέ (enclitic μου, μοι, με), pl. ἡμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς, of person(s) pron. I. (a) The nom. is usually emphatic, when expressed as subjc, as in [[matthew 3 11|Mat.3:11]], [[mark 1 8|Mrk.1:8]], [[luke 3 16|Luk.3:16]], al. But often there is no apparent emphasis, as [[matthew 10 16|Mat.10:16]], [[john 10 17|Jhn.10:17]]; ἰδοὺ ἐ. (= Heb. הִנֵּנִי, cf. [[1-kings 3 8|1Ki.3:8]]), [[acts 9 10|Act.9:10]]; ἐ. (like Heb. אֲנִי), I am, [[john 1 23|Jhn.1:23]] (LXX), [[acts 7 32|Act.7:32]] (LXX). (b) The enclitic forms (see supr.) are used with nouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, where there is no emphasis: ἐν τ. πατρί μου, [[john 14 20|Jhn.14:20;]] μου τ. λόγους, [[matthew 7 24|Mat.7:24;]] ὀπίσω μου, [[matthew 3 11|Mat.3:11;]] ἰσχυρότερός μου, ib.; λέγει μοι, [[revelation 5 5|Rev.5:5;]] also with the prep. πρός, as [[mark 9 19|Mrk.9:19]], al. The full forms (ἐμοῦ, etc.) are used with the other prepositions, as δι᾽ ἐμοῦ, ἐν ἐμοί, εἰς ἐμέ, etc., also for emphasis, as [[luke 10 16|Luk.10:16]], [[john 7 23|Jhn.7:23]], [[mark 14 7|Mrk.14:7]], al. (with) The genitive μου and ἡμῶν are often used for the poss. pronouns ἐμός, ἡμέτερος: τ. λαόν μου, [[matthew 2 6|Mat.2:6;]] μου τῂ ἀπιστιᾳ, [[mark 9 24|Mrk.9:24.]] (d) τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί ( = Heb. מַה־לִי וָלָךְ, [[judges 11 12|Jdg.11:12]], al.), i.e. what have we in common: [[matthew 8 29|Mat.8:29]], [[mark 1 24|Mrk.1:24, 5:7]], [[luke 8 28|Luk.8:28]], [[john 2 4|Jhn.2:4]]; τί γάρ μοι, [[1-corinthians 5 2|1Co.5:2.]] (e) The interchange of ἐγώ and ἡμεῖς, common in π., appears in Pauline Epp. (see M, Pr., 86f., M, Th., 131f.). (f) κἀγώ (= καὶ ἐγώ), and I, even I, I also: [[matthew 2 8|Mat.2:8]], [[luke 2 48|Luk.2:48]], [[john 6 56|Jhn.6:56]], [[romans 3 7|Rom.3:7]], [[1-corinthians 7 40|1Co.7:40]], al.; κἀγώ . . . καί, both . . . and, [[john 7 28|Jhn.7:28.]] (AS)
1. an adulteress , (New Testament):as adjective adulterous , (New Testament) 2. as Substantive = μοιχεία, (New Testament) (ML)

μοιχάω, -ῶ (= cl. μοιχεύω), [in LXX (mid., absol. and with accusative, with party of either sex as subj.) : [[jeremiah 3 8|Jer.3:8 5:7 7:9 9:2 23:14 29:23]], [[ezekiel 16 32|Eze.16:32 23:37, 43]] (נָאַף) * ;] to commit adultery with: with accusative, fem. μοιχεία, -ας, ἡ (μοιχύω), [rn LXX: [[hosea 2 2|Hos.2:2]] (נַאֲפוּף), [[hosea 4 2|Hos.4:2]] (נָאַף), [[jeremiah 13 27|Jer.13:27]] (נִאֻף), Wis.14:26 * ;] adultery: [[john 8 3|Jhn.8:3;]] pl. (see WM, 220; Bl., § 32, 6), [[matthew 15 19|Mat.15:19]], [[mark 7 21|Mrk.7:21]],† (AS)

μοιχεύω (μοιχός), [in LXX: [[exodus 20 13|Exo.20:13]], [[leviticus 20 10|Lev.20:10]], al. (נָאַף) ;] to commit adultery: absol., [[matthew 5 27|Mat.5:27 19:18]], [[mark 10 19|Mrk.10:19]], [[luke 16 18|Luk.16:18 18:20]], [[romans 2 22|Rom.2:22 13:9]], [[james 2 11|Jas.2:11]]; with accusative fem., [[matthew 5 28|Mat.5:28.]] Pass., of the woman, [[matthew 5 32|Mat.5:32 19:9]] WH, mg.), [[john 8 4|Jhn.8:4.]] Metaphorical, of idolatry (see: μιοιχαλίς, and cf. [[jeremiah 3 9|Jer.3:9]], a1.), before μετ᾽ αὐτῆς, [[revelation 2 22|Rev.2:22.]]† (AS)
μοιχός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX for נָאַף ;] an adulterer: [[luke 18 11|Luk.18:11]], [[1-corinthians 6 9|1Co.6:9]], [[hebrews 13 4|Heb.13:4]].† (AS)

μόλις adv. (μόλος, toil) post-Hom. alternative for μόγις, [in LXX: [[proverbs 11 31|Pro.11:31]], Wis.9:16, al. ;] with difficulty, hardly, scarcely: [[luke 9 39|Luk.9:39]] (T, μόγις), [[acts 14 8|Act.14:8 27:7-8, 16]], [[romans 5 7|Rom.5:7]], [[1-peter 4 18|1Pe.4:18]]" (LXX) .† (AS)
Μολόχ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. מֶלֶךְ, prop. מֶלֶךְ King, but vocalized to read בֺּשֶׁת, shame, of. Βάαλ, and see DB, iii, 415 f.), Moloch, the god of the Ammonites : [[acts 7 43|Act.7:43]] (LXX).† (AS)

μολύνω [in LXX: [[genesis 37 31|Gen.37:31]] (טָבַל), [[isaiah 59 3|Isa.59:3]] (גָּאַל ni.), [[zechariah 14 2|Zec.14:2]] (שָׁכַב ni.), Sir.21:28, al. ;] to stain, soil, defile; in NT always symb. and figuratively: [[1-corinthians 8 7|1Co.8:7]], [[revelation 3 4|Rev.3:4 14:4]].† SYN.: μιαίνω, q.v (AS)
μολυσμός, -οῦ, ὁ (μολύνω), [in LXX: [[jeremiah 23 15|Jer.23:15]] (חֲנֻפָה), I [[esther 8 83|Est.8:83]], 2Ma.5:27 * ;] defilement: with genitive obj., [[2-corinthians 7 1|2Co.7:1]] (Plut., FlJ).† (AS)
μομφή, ῆς, ἡ (μέμφομαι), poët. form of μέμψις, blame, com­plaint: [[colossians 3 13|Col.3:13.]]† (AS)

μονογενής, -ές (μόνος, γένος), [in LXX: [[judges 11 34|Jdg.11:34]], [[psalms 22 20|Psa.22:20 25:16 35:17]] (יָחִיד), Tob.3:15 6:10, 14 8:17, Wis.7:22, Bar.4:16 * ;] only, only begotten (DCG, ii, 281), of sons and daughters : [[luke 7 12|Luk.7:12 8:42 9:38]], [[hebrews 11 17|Heb.11:17]]; of Christ, [[john 3 16|Jhn.3:16, 18]], [[1-john 4 9|1Jn.4:9]]; μ. παρὰ πατρός, [[john 1 14|Jhn.1:14;]] μ. θεός, [[john 1 18|Jhn.1:18.]]† (AS)

μόνον, see: μόνος. μόνος, -η, -ον, [in LXX chiefly for לְבַד ;] 1. adj., alone, solitary, forsaken: with verb., [[matthew 14 23|Mat.14:23]], [[mark 6 47|Mrk.6:47]], [[luke 9 36|Luk.9:36]], al.; with pron., [[matthew 18 15|Mat.18:15]], [[mark 9 2|Mrk.9:2]], al.; with subst., [[mark 9 8|Mrk.9:8]], [[luke 4 8|Luk.4:8]], al.; pleonast., οὐκ . . . εἰ μὴ μ., [[matthew 12 4|Mat.12:4]], [[luke 6 4|Luk.6:4]], al.; attrib., only, (ὁ) μ. θεός, [[john 5 44|Jhn.5:44 17:3]], [[romans 16 27|Rom.16:27]], [[1-timothy 1 17|1Ti.1:17]], Ju 25. 2. As adv., (a) neut., (μόνον, alone, only: referring to verb or predic., [[matthew 9 21|Mat.9:21]], [[mark 5 36|Mrk.5:36]], [[james 1 22|Jas.1:22]], al. (see Bl., §44, 2); οὐ (μὴ) μ., [[galatians 4 18|Gal.4:18]], [[james 1 22|Jas.1:22]]; οὐ μ. . . . ἀλλά (Bl, §77, 13.3), [[acts 19 26|Act.19:26]], [[1-john 5 6|1Jn.5:6]], al.; id. before καί (Bl., §81, 1.2), [[romans 5 3|Rom.5:3 9:10]], [[2-corinthians 8 19|2Co.8:19]], al.; (b) κατὰ μόνας, alone (Bl., §44, 1), [[mark 4 10|Mrk.4:10]], [[luke 9 18|Luk.9:18]]. (AS)

μόνος, -η, -ον, [in LXX chiefly for לְבַד ;] 1. adj., alone, solitary, forsaken: with verb., [[matthew 14 23|Mat.14:23]], [[mark 6 47|Mrk.6:47]], [[luke 9 36|Luk.9:36]], al.; with pron., [[matthew 18 15|Mat.18:15]], [[mark 9 2|Mrk.9:2]], al.; with subst., [[mark 9 8|Mrk.9:8]], [[luke 4 8|Luk.4:8]], al.; pleonast., οὐκ . . . εἰ μὴ μ., [[matthew 12 4|Mat.12:4]], [[luke 6 4|Luk.6:4]], al.; attrib., only, (ὁ) μ. θεός, [[john 5 44|Jhn.5:44 17:3]], [[romans 16 27|Rom.16:27]], [[1-timothy 1 17|1Ti.1:17]], Ju 25. 2. As adv., (a) neut., (μόνον, alone, only: referring to verb or predic., [[matthew 9 21|Mat.9:21]], [[mark 5 36|Mrk.5:36]], [[james 1 22|Jas.1:22]], al. (see Bl., §44, 2); οὐ (μὴ) μ., [[galatians 4 18|Gal.4:18]], [[james 1 22|Jas.1:22]]; οὐ μ. . . . ἀλλά (Bl, §77, 13.3), [[acts 19 26|Act.19:26]], [[1-john 5 6|1Jn.5:6]], al.; id. before καί (Bl., §81, 1.2), [[romans 5 3|Rom.5:3 9:10]], [[2-corinthians 8 19|2Co.8:19]], al.; (b) κατὰ μόνας, alone (Bl., §44, 1), [[mark 4 10|Mrk.4:10]], [[luke 9 18|Luk.9:18]]. (AS)
μον-όφθαλμος, -ον (μόνος), Ionic and κοινή, one-eyed, having one eye: [[matthew 18 9|Mat.18:9]], [[mark 9 47|Mrk.9:47]].† (AS)
μονόω, -ῶ (μόνος), [in Aq.: [[genesis 49 6|Gen.49:6]] ;] to leave alone, forsake: of a childless widow, pf. ptcp. pass., [[1-timothy 5 5|1Ti.5:5.]]† (AS)

μορφή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX: [[judges 8 18|Jdg.8:18]] A (תֹּאַר), [[job 4 16|Job.4:16]] (תְּמוּנָה), [[isaiah 44 13|Isa.44:13]] (תַּבְנִית), Dan LXX 3:19 (צֶלֶם), Da TH [[daniel 4 33|Dan.4:33 5:6, 9-10 7:28]] (זִיו), Tob.1:13, Wis.18:1, 4Ma.15:4 * ;] form, shape, appearance (Hom., Eur., . sch., al.); in philos. lang. the specific character or essential form (Arist., see Gifford, Inc., 26 ff.) : [[mark 16 12|Mrk.16:12]], [[philippians 2 6|Php.2:6-7]].† SYN.: μόρφωσις, the outline, delineation, semblance of the μορφή, as distinct from the μ. itself (Lft., Notes, 262); σχῆμα, shape, fashion, disting. from μορφή as the outward and accidental from the inward and essential (cf. Tr., Syn., § LXX; Lft., Phi., 125 ff.; Gifford., Inc., l.with) (AS)
μορφόω, -ῶ (μορφή), [in Aq.: [[isaiah 44 13|Isa.44:13]] * ;] to form: figuratively, [[galatians 4 19|Gal.4:19]] (cf. μετα-, συμ-μορφόω) (AS)

μόρφωσις, -εως, ἡ (μορφόω), 1. a forming, shaping (Theophr.). 2. form, outline, semblance: [[romans 2 20|Rom.2:20;]] opposite to δύναμις, [[2-timothy 3 5|2Ti.3:5.]]† SYN.: μορφή (which see), σχῆμα (AS)
μοσχο-ποιέω, -ῶ to make a calf (as an image) : [[acts 7 41|Act.7:41]] (LXX, ἐποίησε μόσχον).† (AS)

μόσχος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for פַּר, also for שׁוֹר, עֵגֶל. etc. ;] 1. a young shoot or twig. 2. ὁ, ἡ, μ., offspring; (a) of men; (b) of animals; most frequently (as always in LXX), a calf, bullock, heifer: [[luke 15 23|Luk.15:23, 27 15:30]], [[hebrews 9 12|Heb.9:12, 19]] [[revelation 4 7|Rev.4:7]].† (AS)

μόχθος, -ου, ὁ (= Hom. μόγος), in cl. chiefly poët., [in LXX for תְּלָאָה, עָמָל, etc. ;] toil, labour, hardship, distress: [[2-corinthians 11 27|2Co.11:27]], [[1-thessalonians 2 9|1Th.2:9]], [[2-thessalonians 3 8|2Th.3:8]].† SYN.: κόπος (which see), πόνος (AS)

ἐγώ, genitive, etc., ἐμοῦ, ἐμοί, ἐμέ (enclitic μου, μοι, με), pl. ἡμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς, of person(s) pron. I. (a) The nom. is usually emphatic, when expressed as subjc, as in [[matthew 3 11|Mat.3:11]], [[mark 1 8|Mrk.1:8]], [[luke 3 16|Luk.3:16]], al. But often there is no apparent emphasis, as [[matthew 10 16|Mat.10:16]], [[john 10 17|Jhn.10:17]]; ἰδοὺ ἐ. (= Heb. הִנֵּנִי, cf. [[1-kings 3 8|1Ki.3:8]]), [[acts 9 10|Act.9:10]]; ἐ. (like Heb. אֲנִי), I am, [[john 1 23|Jhn.1:23]] (LXX), [[acts 7 32|Act.7:32]] (LXX). (b) The enclitic forms (see supr.) are used with nouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, where there is no emphasis: ἐν τ. πατρί μου, [[john 14 20|Jhn.14:20;]] μου τ. λόγους, [[matthew 7 24|Mat.7:24;]] ὀπίσω μου, [[matthew 3 11|Mat.3:11;]] ἰσχυρότερός μου, ib.; λέγει μοι, [[revelation 5 5|Rev.5:5;]] also with the prep. πρός, as [[mark 9 19|Mrk.9:19]], al. The full forms (ἐμοῦ, etc.) are used with the other prepositions, as δι᾽ ἐμοῦ, ἐν ἐμοί, εἰς ἐμέ, etc., also for emphasis, as [[luke 10 16|Luk.10:16]], [[john 7 23|Jhn.7:23]], [[mark 14 7|Mrk.14:7]], al. (with) The genitive μου and ἡμῶν are often used for the poss. pronouns ἐμός, ἡμέτερος: τ. λαόν μου, [[matthew 2 6|Mat.2:6;]] μου τῂ ἀπιστιᾳ, [[mark 9 24|Mrk.9:24.]] (d) τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί ( = Heb. מַה־לִי וָלָךְ, [[judges 11 12|Jdg.11:12]], al.), i.e. what have we in common: [[matthew 8 29|Mat.8:29]], [[mark 1 24|Mrk.1:24, 5:7]], [[luke 8 28|Luk.8:28]], [[john 2 4|Jhn.2:4]]; τί γάρ μοι, [[1-corinthians 5 2|1Co.5:2.]] (e) The interchange of ἐγώ and ἡμεῖς, common in π., appears in Pauline Epp. (see M, Pr., 86f., M, Th., 131f.). (f) κἀγώ (= καὶ ἐγώ), and I, even I, I also: [[matthew 2 8|Mat.2:8]], [[luke 2 48|Luk.2:48]], [[john 6 56|Jhn.6:56]], [[romans 3 7|Rom.3:7]], [[1-corinthians 7 40|1Co.7:40]], al.; κἀγώ . . . καί, both . . . and, [[john 7 28|Jhn.7:28.]] (AS)

μουσικός, -ή, -όν [in LXX: [[genesis 31 27|Gen.31:27]], [[ezekiel 26 13|Eze.26:13]] (שִׁיר), Dan LXX TH [[daniel 3 5|Dan.3:5]] ff. (זְמָר), Sir.22:6, al. ;] skilled in the arts, esp. in music; as subst., ὁ μ., a minstrel, musician: [[revelation 18 22|Rev.18:22.]]† (AS)
μυελός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX: [[genesis 45 18|Gen.45:18]] (חֶלֶב), [[job 21 24|Job.21:24]] (מֹחַ) [[job 33 24|Job.33:24]] * ;] marrow: [[hebrews 4 12|Heb.4:12.]]† (AS)

μυέω, -ῶ (μύω, to shut the mouth), [in LXX: 3Ma.2:30 * ;] to initiate into the mysteries (so chiefly in cl.; LXX, l.with); hence, to instruct: pass., [[philippians 4 12|Php.4:12]] (RV, I have learned the secret).† (AS)

μῦθος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Wis.17:4 A, Sir.20:19 * ;] 1. speech, con­versation. 2. (a) a story, narrative (Hom.); (b) later, opposite to λόγος (a true narrative) = Lat. fabula, a myth, fable, fiction: [[1-timothy 1 4|1Ti.1:4 4:7]], [[2-timothy 4 4|2Ti.4:4]], [[titus 1 14|Tit.1:14]], [[2-peter 1 16|2Pe.1:16]].† SYN.. λόγος, q.v (AS)
μυκάσμαι, -ῶμαι in cl. chiefly poët., [in Sm.: [[job 6 5|Job.6:5]] * ;] prop., of oxen (onomatop.), to low, bellow; of a lion, to roar: [[revelation 10 3|Rev.10:3.]]† (AS)

μυκτηρίζω (μυκτήρ, the nose), [in LXX: 4Ki.19:21, [[job 22 19|Job.22:19]], [[psalms 80 6|Psa.80:6]], al. (לָעַג), [[proverbs 1 30|Pro.1:30]] (נָאַץ) [[proverbs 15 20|Pro.15:20]] (בָּזָה), 1Ma.7:34, al. ;] to turn up the nose or sneer at, mock: pass., [[galatians 6 7|Gal.6:7]] (cf. ἐκ-μυκτηρίζω).† (AS)
μυλικός, -ή, -όν (μύλη, a mill), of a mill: λίθος μ., [[luke 17 2|Luk.17:2.]]† (AS)

μύλος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX for רֵחֶה, [[numbers 11 8|Num.11:8]], [[deuteronomy 24 6|Deu.24:6]], al. ;] 1. = μύλη, a mill (Strab., Plut., LXX) : [[matthew 24 41|Mat.24:41]], [[revelation 18 22|Rev.18:22]]. 2. a mill-stone (Anth.) : [[revelation 18 21|Rev.18:21]] (T); μ. ὀνικός, [[matthew 18 6|Mat.18:6]], [[mark 9 42|Mrk.9:42]] (see Swete, in l).† (AS)
μυλών, -ῶος, ὁ [in LXX: [[jeremiah 52 11|Jer.52:11]] * ;] a mill-house: [[matthew 24 41|Mat.24:41]] (Rec.; μύλος, WH, R).† (AS)
Μύρα, Μύρρα (LT, Tr., WH), -ων, τά, Myra, a city of Lycia : [[acts 27 5|Act.27:5.]]† (AS)

μυριάς, -άδος, ἡ (μυρίος), [in LXX chiefly for רְבָבָה ;] ten thousand, a myriad: pl., [[acts 19 19|Act.19:19]], [[revelation 5 11|Rev.5:11 9:16]]; hyperb., of vast numbers, [[luke 12 1|Luk.12:1]], [[acts 21 20|Act.21:20]], [[hebrews 12 12|Heb.12:12]], Ju 14.† (AS)
μυρίζω (μύρον), Ionic and poët. (comic), to anoint: [[mark 14 8|Mrk.14:8.]]† SYN.: see: ἀλείφω, and cf. μύρον (AS)
μυρίος, -α, -ον 1. numberless, countless, infinite: [[1-corinthians 4 15|1Co.4:15 14:19]]. 2. As a definite numeral, in pl., μύριοι, -αι, -α, ten thousand: [[matthew 18 24|Mat.18:24.]]† (AS)

μύρον, -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for שֶׁמֶן, [[proverbs 27 9|Pro.27:9]], [[psalms 133 2|Psa.133:2]], al. ;] ointment: [[matthew 26 7|Mat.26:7, 12]], [[mark 14 3|Mrk.14:3-5]], [[luke 7 37|Luk.7:37-38, 46 23:56]], [[john 11 2|Jhn.11:2 12:3, 5]], [[revelation 18 13|Rev.18:13]].† SYN.: ἔλαιον, q.v (AS)
Μυσία, -ας, ἡ Mysia, a province of Asia Minor: [[acts 16 7|Act.16:7-8.]]† (AS)

μυστήρισν, -ου, τό (μυέω), [in LXX: Dan LXX TH [[daniel 2 18|Dan.2:18]] ff. (רָז), Tob.12:7, 11, Jdth.2:2, Wis.2:22 6:22 14:15, 23, Sir.3:18 22:22 27:16-17, 21, 2Ma.13:21 * ;] 1. that which is known to the μύστης (initiated), a mystery or secret doctrine, mostly in pl., τὰ μ. (Æsch., Hdt., al.). 2. In later writers (Menand., Incert., 168), that which may not be revealed (not, however, as in the modern sense, intrinsically difficult to understand), a secret or mystery of any kind (To, Jth, 2Mac, ll, with). 3. In NT, of the counsels of God (cf. Th.: [[job 15 8|Job.15:8]], [[psalms 25 14|Psa.25:14]] for סוֹד), once hidden but now revealed in the Gospel or some fact thereof; (a) of the Christian revelation generally : [[romans 16 25|Rom.16:25]], [[1-corinthians 2 7|1Co.2:7]], [[colossians 1 26|Col.1:26-27]], [[ephesians 3 3|Eph.3:3]], 9; τ. βασιλείας τ. θεοῦ, [[mark 4 11|Mrk.4:11;]] τ. θεοῦ, [[1-corinthians 2 1|1Co.2:1]], [[revelation 10 7|Rev.10:7]]; τ. θ., Χριστοῦ, [[colossians 2 2|Col.2:2;]] τ. Χριστοῦ., [[colossians 4 3|Col.4:3]], [[ephesians 3 4|Eph.3:4]]; τ. θελήματος αὐτοῦ, [[ephesians 1 9|Eph.1:9;]] τ. εὐαγγελίον, [[ephesians 6 19|Eph.6:19;]] τ. πίστεως, [[1-timothy 3 9|1Ti.3:9;]] τ. εὐσεβείας, [[1-timothy 3 16|1Ti.3:16;]] (b) of particular truths, or details, of the Christian revelation : [[romans 11 25|Rom.11:25]], [[1-corinthians 15 51|1Co.15:51]], [[ephesians 5 32|Eph.5:32]], [[2-thessalonians 2 7|2Th.2:7]], [[revelation 1 20|Rev.1:20 17:5, 7]]; pl., τὰ μ., [[1-corinthians 13 2|1Co.13:2 14:2]]; θεοῦ, [[1-corinthians 4 1|1Co.4:1;]] τ. βασιλείας τ. οὐρανῶν (θεοῦ), [[matthew 13 11|Mat.13:11]], [[luke 8 10|Luk.8:10]] (cf. Westc., Eph., 180 ff.; AR, Eph., 234 ff.; Lft., Col., 165 f.; Hatch, Essays, 57 f.; DB, iii, 465 ff.; DCG, ii, 213 ff.).† (AS)
μυ-ωπάζω (μύωψ, closing the eyes, short-sighted; μύω, ὤψ) to be short-sighted: [[2-peter 1 9|2Pe.1:9]] (R, mg., closing his eyes; see ICC, in l).† (AS)
μώλωψ, -ωπος, ὁ [in LXX for חַבּוּרָה, [[exodus 21 25|Exo.21:25]], al. ;] a bruise, wound from a stripe: [[1-peter 2 24|1Pe.2:24]] (LXX) (Arist., Plut., al.).† (AS)

μωμάομαι, -ῶμαι (μῶμος), poët. and late prose, [in LXX: [[proverbs 9 7|Pro.9:7]] (מאוּם), Wis.10:14, Sir.31:18 * ;] to find fault with, blame: [[2-corinthians 8 20|2Co.8:20;]] pass., [[2-corinthians 6 3|2Co.6:3.]]† (AS)

μῶμος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX, of physical blemishes : [[leviticus 21 17|Lev.21:17]] ff., [[deuteronomy 15 21|Deu.15:21]], [[song-of-solomon 4 7|Sng.4:7]], al. (מאוּם); of mental defect, Sir.20:24, al. ;] 1. in cl. poets and late prose, blame, disgrace. 2. In LXX, perb. because of resemblance to a physical blemish (cf. ἄμωμος, [[1-peter 1 19|1Pe.1:19]], and see Hort., in l); metaphorically, of licentious persons, [[2-peter 2 13|2Pe.2:13.]]† (AS)

μωραίνω (μωρός), [in LXX: [[isaiah 19 11|Isa.19:11]], [[jeremiah 10 14|Jer.10:14 51:17]] (בָּעַר ni.), [[2-kings 24 10|2Ki.24:10]], [[isaiah 44 25|Isa.44:25]] R (שָׂכַל ni., pi.)* ;] 1. cl., to be foolish, play the fool. 2. LXX and NT, causal, to make foolish: [[1-corinthians 1 20|1Co.1:20;]] pass., to become foolish: [[romans 1 22|Rom.1:22;]] of salt that has lost its flavour, become tasteless: [[matthew 5 13|Mat.5:13]], [[luke 14 34|Luk.14:34]].† (AS)
μωρία, -ας, ἡ (μωρός), [in LXX: Sir.20:31 * ;] foolishness: [[1-corinthians 1 18|1Co.1:18 1:21 1:23 2:14 3:19]].† (AS)
silly talking , (New Testament) from μωρολόγος (ML)

μωρός, -ά, -όν [in LXX for נָבָל, etc.; frequently in Sir. ;] 1. prop., of the nerves, dull, sluggish (Hipp., Arist.). 2. Of the mind, dull, stupid, foolish: [[matthew 5 22|Mat.5:22]] (see Field, Notes, 3 ff.) [[matthew 7 26|Mat.7:26 23:17, 19]] (T, WH, txt., R, om.) [[matthew 25 2|Mat.25:2-3]], 8, [[1-corinthians 3 18|1Co.3:18 4:10]]; of things, παράδοσις, [[mark 7 13|Mrk.7:13]] (T, WH, txt., R, om.) : ζητήσεις, [[2-timothy 2 23|2Ti.2:23]], [[titus 3 9|Tit.3:9]]; τὸ μ. τ. θεοῦ, [[1-corinthians 1 25|1Co.1:25;]] τὰ μ. τ. κόσμου, [[1-corinthians 1 27|1Co.1:27.]]† (AS)

Μωυσῆς (Μωϋσῆς, T; Μωσῆς, Rec.), -έως, dative - (as LXX: [[exodus 5 20|Exo.5:20]], al.), and -εῖ, accusative -ῆν (ac LXX) and -έα ([[luke 16 29|Luk.16:29]] only) (Heb. מֹשֶׁה), Moses: [[matthew 8 4|Mat.8:4 17:3-4]], al.; νόμος Μωυσέως, [[luke 2 22|Luk.2:22 24:44]], [[john 7 23|Jhn.7:23]], [[acts 13 39|Act.13:39 15:5 28:23]], [[1-corinthians 9 9|1Co.9:9]], [[hebrews 10 28|Heb.10:28]]; by meton., of the books of Moses, [[luke 16 29|Luk.16:29 24:27]], [[acts 15 21|Act.15:21]], [[2-corinthians 3 15|2Co.3:15]] (AS)
Ναασσών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. נַחְשׁוֹן), Naasson: [[matthew 1 4|Mat.1:4]], [[luke 3 32|Luk.3:32]].† (AS)
Ναγγαί, ὁ indecl., Naggai: [[luke 3 25|Luk.3:25.]]† (AS)

Ναζαρά ([[matthew 4 13|Mat.4:13]]­ L, -άθ­[[luke 4 16|Luk.4:16]]) Ναζαρέθ ([[matthew 21 11|Mat.21:11]], [[acts 10 38|Act.10:38]]), Ναζαρέτ (so always Rec.; WH, in foll, instances, where -έθ, T), ἡ, indecl. (Semitic form uncertain), Nazareth: [[matthew 2 23|Mat.2:23]], [[mark 1 9|Mrk.1:9]], [[luke 1 26|Luk.1:26 2:4, 39 2:51]], [[john 1 45|Jhn.1:45-46]].† (AS)
Ναζαρηνός, -οῦ, ὁ (on the Semitic form, see Dalman, Gr., 141 n.) a Nazarene: [[mark 1 24|Mrk.1:24 10:47 14:67 16:6]], [[luke 4 34|Luk.4:34 24:19]].† (AS)
Ναθάμ (Rec. Ναθάν), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נָתַן), Nathan: [[luke 3 31|Luk.3:31.]]† (AS)
Ναθαναήλ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. נְתַנְאֵל), Nathaniel, prob. to be identified with Bartholomew (which see): [[john 1 45|Jhn.1:45-49 21:2]].† (AS)

ναί particle of affirmation, yea, verily, even so; in answer to a question: [[matthew 9 28|Mat.9:28 13:51 17:25 21:16]], [[john 11 27|Jhn.11:27 21:15-16]], [[acts 5 8|Act.5:8 22:27]], [[romans 3 29|Rom.3:29]]; before λέγω ὑμῖν, [[matthew 11 9|Mat.11:9]], [[luke 7 26|Luk.7:26]]; repeated for emphasis, ναὶ ναί (opposite to oὒ oὔ): [[matthew 5 37|Mat.5:37;]] ἤτω ὑμῶν τὸ ναὶ ναί, [[james 5 12|Jas.5:12;]] ν. καὶ οὔ, [[2-corinthians 1 18|2Co.1:18-19;]] ἵνα ᾖ . . . τὸ ναὶ ναί, [[2-corinthians 1 17|2Co.1:17;]] τὸ ν., [[2-corinthians 1 20|2Co.1:20;]] in assent to an assertion: [[matthew 15 27|Mat.15:27]], [[mark 7 28|Mrk.7:28]], [[revelation 14 13|Rev.14:13 16:7]]; in confirmation of a previous assertion: [[matthew 11 26|Mat.11:26]], [[luke 10 21|Luk.10:21 11:51 12:5]], [[philippians 4 3|Php.4:3]], Phm 20; in solemn asseveration [[revelation 1 7|Rev.1:7 22:20]].† (AS)
Ναίν (Rec. Ναΐν), ἡ, indecl. (Heb. נָאָה), Nain, a village of Galilee: [[luke 7 11|Luk.7:11.]]† (AS)

ναός, -οῦ, ὁ (Att.. νεώς; ναίω, to inhabit), [in LXX (νεώς, 2Ma.6:2, al.) chiefly for הֵיכָל ;] 1. a temple (Hom., Find., al.). 2. The inmost part of a temple, the shrine (Hat., Xen., al.); in NT, (a) generally: pl., [[acts 17 24|Act.17:24;]] of silver models of a heathen shrine, [[acts 19 24|Act.19:24;]] (b) of the temple building proper, or sanctuary, at Jerusalem, as distinct from τ. ἱερόν (which see), the whole temple enclosure: [[matthew 23 16|Mat.23:16-17, 35 27:5, 40]], [[mark 14 58|Mrk.14:58 15:29]] [[john 2 19|Jhn.2:19-20]], [[revelation 11 2|Rev.11:2]]; (τοῦ) θεοῦ, [[matthew 26 61|Mat.26:61 27:51]], [[mark 15 38|Mrk.15:38]], [[luke 1 9|Luk.1:9, 21-22 23:45]], [[1-corinthians 3 17|1Co.3:17]], [[2-corinthians 6 16|2Co.6:16]], [[2-thessalonians 2 4|2Th.2:4]], [[revelation 11 1|Rev.11:1]]; of the temple in the Apocal. visions, [[revelation 3 12|Rev.3:12 7:15 11:19 14:15, 17 15:5-6, 8 16:1, 17 21:22]] a. Metaphorical, of Christians, [[1-corinthians 3 16|1Co.3:16 6:19]], [[2-corinthians 6 16|2Co.6:16]], [[ephesians 2 21|Eph.2:21]]; of Christ's body, [[john 2 21|Jhn.2:21]] (cf. [[john 2 19|Jhn.2:19]]); ὁ θεὸς ν. αὐτῆς ἐστιν, [[revelation 21 22|Rev.21:22]] b.† SYN.: ἱερόν (AS)
Ναούμ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. נַחוּם;), Nahum: [[luke 3 25|Luk.3:25.]]† (AS)

νάρδος, -ου, ἡ (Heb. נֵרְדְּ, both from Sanscrit narda, see Boisacq, see word), [in LXX: [[song-of-solomon 1 12|Sng.1:12 4:13-14]] (נֵרְדְּ)* ;] nard; (a) an Indian plant, the Nardostachys nardus jatamansi, used for the preparation of a fragrant ointment; (b) ointment of nard: [[mark 14 3|Mrk.14:3]], [[john 12 3|Jhn.12:3]].† (AS)
the narcissus , (Homeric Hymns), etc. From ναρκάω, because of its narcotic properties. (ML)
ναυαγέω, -ῶ (ναῦς, + ἄγνυμι, to break) to suffer shipwreck: [[2-corinthians 11 25|2Co.11:25;]] metaphorically, before περὶ τ. πίστιν, [[1-timothy 1 19|1Ti.1:19.]]† (AS)
ναύ-κληρος, -ου, ὁ (ναῦς, κλῆρος), a shipowner, shipmaster: [[acts 27 11|Act.27:11.]]† (AS)
ναῦς, νεώς accusative ναῦν, ἡ, [in LXX for עָנִי, אֲנִיָּה ;] a ship: [[acts 27 41|Act.27:41]] (elsewhere in NT always τ. πλοῖον; see M, [[proverbs 25 1|Pro.25:1-28]] f.; Bl., Gosp., 186 f.).† (AS)
ναύτης, -ου, ὁ (ναῦς), [in Aq.: [[ezekiel 27 9|Eze.27:9;]] Sm.: [[ezekiel 27 29|Eze.27:29]] * ;] a seaman, sailor: [[acts 27 27|Act.27:27, 30]], [[revelation 18 17|Rev.18:17]].† (AS)
Ναχώρ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. נָחוֹר), Nahor: [[luke 3 34|Luk.3:34.]]† (AS)
νεανίας, -ου, ὁ (νεάν = νέος) [in LXX for נַעַר, בָּחוּר ;] a young man: [[acts 7 58|Act.7:58 20:9 23:17-18]].† (AS)

νεανίσκος, -ου, ὁ (dimin. of νεανίας) [in LXX chiefly for נַעַר, also for בָּחוּר, etc. ;] a young man, youth: [[matthew 19 20|Mat.19:20, 22]], [[mark 14 51|Mrk.14:51 16:5]], [[luke 7 14|Luk.7:14]], [[acts 2 17|Act.2:17]]" (LXX) [[acts 23 18|Act.23:18, 22]], [[1-john 2 13|1Jn.2:13-14]]; of an attendant (cf. [[genesis 14 24|Gen.14:24]], al.) : [[acts 5 10|Act.5:10]].† (AS)
Νεάπολις, -εως, ἡ Rec. for Νέα Πόλις (WH), the more frequently form (LS, see word), Neapolis, a maritime city of Macedonia: [[acts 16 11|Act.16:11.]]† (AS)
Ναιμάν (Rec. Νεεμάν), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נַעֲמָן), Naaman: [[luke 4 27|Luk.4:27.]]† (AS)

νεκρός, -α, -ον, [in LXX chiefly for מֵת ;] dead, I. as adj., 1. prop.: [[acts 5 10|Act.5:10 20:9]], [[james 2 26|Jas.2:26]], [[revelation 1 18|Rev.1:18]], al.; ὡσεὶ ν., [[matthew 28 4|Mat.28:4]], [[mark 9 26|Mrk.9:26]], [[revelation 1 17|Rev.1:17]]; of that which is subject to death, [[romans 8 10|Rom.8:10.]] 2. Metaphorical, (a) of persons: [[luke 15 24|Luk.15:24, 32]]; of those immersed in worldly cares, [[matthew 8 22|Mat.8:22]], [[luke 9 60|Luk.9:60]]; of spiritual death, [[john 5 25|Jhn.5:25]], [[romans 6 13|Rom.6:13]], [[ephesians 5 14|Eph.5:14]], [[revelation 3 1|Rev.3:1]]; τ. παραπτώμασιν, [[ephesians 2 1|Eph.2:1]], 5 [[colossians 2 13|Col.2:13]]; of the opposite condition, ν. τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, [[romans 6 11|Rom.6:11;]] (b) of things regarded as inoperative, devoid of power: ἁμαρτία, [[romans 7 8|Rom.7:8;]] πίστις, [[james 2 17|Jas.2:17, 26]]; ἔργα, [[hebrews 6 1|Heb.6:1 9:14]]. II. As subst., νεκρός, ὁ (Hom., al.), chiefly in pl. (οἱ) ν., the dead: [[matthew 11 5|Mat.11:5]], [[mark 12 26|Mrk.12:26]], [[luke 20 37|Luk.20:37]], [[1-corinthians 15 15|1Co.15:15]], al.; ἀνάστασις (τ.) νεκρῶν, [[matthew 22 31|Mat.22:31]], [[acts 17 32|Act.17:32]], al.; ν. . . . ζῶντες, [[matthew 22 32|Mat.22:32]], [[mark 12 27|Mrk.12:27]], [[acts 10 42|Act.10:42]], al.; ἀπὸ νεκρῶν, [[luke 16 30|Luk.16:30;]] ἐκ ν., [[mark 6 14|Mrk.6:14]], [[luke 24 46|Luk.24:46]], [[john 12 1|Jhn.12:1]], [[acts 13 34|Act.13:34]], [[romans 10 7|Rom.10:7]], al.; πρωτότοκος ἐκ τῶν ν., [[colossians 1 18|Col.1:18;]] ζωὴ ἐκ ν., [[romans 11 15|Rom.11:15;]] constr. praegn., ἐκ ν. ζῶντες, [[romans 6 13|Rom.6:13.]] (AS)

νεκρόω, ῶ (νεκρός), to make dead, put to death; pass., to be dead: hyperbolically, of impotent age, [[hebrews 11 12|Heb.11:12;]] σῶμα, [[romans 4 19|Rom.4:19.]] Trop., of carnal impulses, τὰ μέλη, [[colossians 3 5|Col.3:5.]]† (AS)
